inputs_used: content-system/seo/link-map.csv (grep greece, getting married in greece, CNI, apostille, register, concierge, magazine)

payload.title: How Do You Get Married in Greece?
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more who are drawn to Greece and want one clear answer to 'how do we actually get married there': whether their marriage will be legal, symbolic or religious, which documents they need from Australia and in what order, what happens at the municipality and how the marriage is recognised back home, and then which island, month and venue style suit them, so they can decide Greece is workable and hand the planning to someone who will look after it.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation at /wonderland-concierge so an advisor can shape the island, venue, travel and guest stays around the route they choose.
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'getting married in greece' mostly lead with island inspiration and venue lists, bury or blur the legal process, and mix Greek, UK and US paperwork rules with unattributed lead times and fees. This pillar answers the head question in order for Australians: first the three routes (legal civil, symbolic, Greek Orthodox), then the legal steps from an Australian starting point (Certificate of No Impediment and documents, translation and Apostille, the civil ceremony at the municipality, registration in Greece and recognition at home), with lead times only where an official source states them. Church rules are credited to the Archdiocese, timing uses station-labelled figures with no best month, and each island gets one or two honest lines. Every deeper question routes once to the dedicated sister guide, so the reader gets the whole map on one page and the detail one click away.
must_include: Intro answering the head question in the first 100 words (you can marry legally in Greece in a civil ceremony at the municipality, hold a symbolic ceremony, or marry in a Greek Orthodox church; legal steps come first), then exactly 4 Key takeaways, one sentence each, none naming a best month, island or venue.

Legal, symbolic or religious: the three routes, what each means for legal recognition, and who each suits; neutral one line linking /destination-weddings/same-sex-marriage-greece (no legal position stated).

Step by step for Australians: (1) Certificate of No Impediment and documents, linking /expert-advice/what-is-a-certificate-of-no-impediment-and-who-issues-it; (2) translation and Apostille, linking /expert-advice/what-is-an-apostille-and-does-my-paperwork-need-one; (3) civil ceremony at the municipality (who officiates, witnesses, 'a fee applies' only where sourced); (4) registration in Greece and recognition back home, linking /expert-advice/do-you-have-to-register-an-overseas-marriage-at-home. Lead times only as an official source states them, otherwise [[VERIFY]]. Steps from official Australian (DFAT, Smartraveller) and Greek government sources only.

Greek Orthodox wedding in brief: eligibility and paperwork outline with church rules credited to the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia ('ask your priest for Greece'); link /destination-weddings/greek-orthodox-wedding for the full guide.
When to marry: a short summary with station-labelled HNMS figures only, no best month, closed periods credited to the Archdiocese; link /destination-weddings/best-time-to-get-married-in-greece.

Choose your island: Santorini, Mykonos, Crete, Rhodes, Corfu and Paros in one or two lines each, no ranking. Link once each: /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding, /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding, /destination-weddings/wedding-in-crete, /destination-weddings/santorini-or-mykonos-wedding, /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/crete-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/rhodes-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/corfu-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/paros-wedding-venues.

Venues and packages: a short orientation with no venue entries and no prices; link once each /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages, /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages-all-inclusive, /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-packages, /destination-weddings/crete-wedding-packages, and the live hub /destinations/europe/greece (which owns venue intent). This section carries the ONLY Advisor line in the body (brand-facts.md claims only, about planning, never legal, church or religious paperwork help), linking /wonderland-concierge.
Traditions: two or three sentences linking /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions.

FAQ (4 to 6), for example: Is a Greek wedding legally recognised in Australia? Do we need a Certificate of No Impediment to marry in Greece? Can non-Orthodox couples marry in a Greek church? Can we have a symbolic ceremony instead? How far ahead should we start the paperwork (only as sourced)? Answers from the same sources as the body.

Close: the one Advisor line from brand-facts.md (never the definition line or 'last dance'). Links: /wonderland-concierge as the main CTA (anchor names 'Wedded Concierge'), /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-greece&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing on /wonderland-concierge and /magazine only. All 19 sister URLs linked exactly once across the body.
avoid: Any price, fee amount, cost range or 'free'; only 'a fee applies' where an official source says so.
'Best' ranking of islands or venues, or naming a best month (title and keyword aside).
Any same-sex legal position or commentary beyond the single neutral linking line.
Lead times, processing times, document validity periods or residency requirements not from an official source; UK or US paperwork rules presented as Australian.

Advisor or Wedded Concierge help with legal, church or religious paperwork; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; more than one Advisor line in the body besides the close; the definition line and 'last dance'; 'Wonderland Concierge' as anchor text.
Wedded Privileges, transfers, drive, ferry or flight times; business details (named Advisor, phone line) which are deferred.
Repeating venue entries, listings or capacities from the venue guides or the hub.
Church rules not credited to the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia; religious commentary.
Research talk in copy ('we could not confirm', 'according to our research'); hedge stacking.
Competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs or their wording and images.
Clichés (fairytale, dream day, breathtaking), exclamation marks, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding.
payload.cannibalisation_check: No URL in content-system/seo/link-map.csv targets 'getting married in greece' as its primary keyword. /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues lists 'getting married in greece' as a secondary/cluster term but owns 'greece wedding venues'; this pillar owns the head question and legal process, holds no venue entries, and links to it once. /destinations/europe/greece (live hub) owns venue intent; the pillar links to it and does not compete for venue terms. /destination-weddings/best-time-to-get-married-in-greece owns timing, /destination-weddings/greek-orthodox-wedding owns Orthodox requirements, /destination-weddings/same-sex-marriage-greece owns same-sex law; the pillar summarises and links down. Editor to add an up-link to this pillar from each sister. SEO to check variants (how to get married in greece, legal requirements to marry in greece, greece wedding requirements for australians).
